title: Giving Benny Carter his first trumpet mouthpiece
summary: At the Cotton Pickers he encouraged Carter to take up trumpet and gave him his first mouthpiece.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well, I do it by practicing every day, and by listening. I don't listen to -- I listen to the new trumpet players all the time. The guys that I like, as I say, Clifford Brown, I admired him and I study him, I study his records every day and I see the things that he's doing that were not done back in the '20's. And I used to -- and I listen to other trumpet players. I run into quite a few great trumpet players, say Bobby Hackett, for instance, will -- he's slowed down a little bit, but he has something and I listen to all of them. Even Benny Carter, Benny Carter and I
were great friends, you know, and I think I was responsible for Benny Carter taking up trumpet. I gave him his first mouthpiece.

I did. I gave Benny his first mouthpiece. We were with the Cotton Pickers and he was saying, I think I'm going to play trumpet. And I say, why not. He says, well, I can play the saxophone, he say, won't that affect my lip? I said, no, because I play saxophone and trumpet all the same time and I encourd him to do it. And so I gave him his first mouthpiece. And he wanted to play trumpet one day, and I said, come on and play and so he picked up his trumpet and started to play. He'll tell you the same thing today.
